problem: End-to-end RL navigation policies for legged robots still depend on continuously updated robot-to-goal states from external localization or state estimation, leaving goal tracking outside the learned policy. Purely local RL policies also make myopic decisions and get trapped in dead ends under partial observability.
motivation: Legged robots in confined, occluded environments with dead ends need long-horizon spatial context, not only reactive avoidance. Proprioceptive histories from joint encoders and IMU carry egomotion information, so the paper asks whether a policy can maintain its relation to the goal internally when the goal is given only once at episode start.
key_idea: Train an end-to-end RL policy on multi-frequency proprioceptive history and temporal depth, with an auxiliary spatial-anchor head that predicts relative goal, relative spawn position and body velocity, so the goal need only be provided at initialization.
insight: The 200 Hz high-frequency proprioception stream is essential: without it, SR collapses to about 0% and goal/spawn prediction errors rise to roughly 3 m. Directly learning anchors jointly with the policy beats integrating a pretrained odometry model (GUIDE-Legolas: SR 82.5 vs 99.9 on Cluttered Easy), because accumulated drift hurts. The small gap to GT-oracle variants shows the learned internal state is nearly sufficient. The velocity head matters most for the hard maze (SR 53.5 without it), and the multi-critic split of sparse and dense rewards is also needed (49.1 without it).
method: Goal-initialized POMDP: the goal g^0 is given once in the egocentric frame and no updates follow; the policy conditions on o_t, history and predicted context ĉ_t.

Multi-frequency proprioception encoder: a 10 Hz stream (N=10) and a 200 Hz stream (M=20 per interval) are each processed with self-attention, fused into one token sequence, then passed through a GRU to give the proprioception token z^p.

Spatial anchor predictor: three MLP heads on z^p predict body velocity, relative goal and relative spawn position. They are supervised with privileged sim states (MSE for velocity, Huber for positions) and their outputs feed the actor.
Depth processing: an 8-frame 30x43 depth buffer goes through a shared CNN and temporal self-attention; cross-attention with z^p as query, followed by a GRU, gives the spatial latent z^s.
Actor: takes [z^s, v̂, ĝ, ŝ, latest proprioception] and outputs twist commands at 10 Hz for a 50 Hz low-level locomotion controller (Long et al.).
Asymmetric multi-critic PPO: the critic sees privileged occupancy and explored-region maps; separate sparse-task and dense-shaping value heads are combined into one normalized advantage.
Procedural curriculum: cluttered terrains (alleys, L-corners, pillars) and DFS perfect mazes, with growing complexity and start-goal distance; maze progress reward uses graph connectivity distance.

setting.backbone: Custom transformer/CNN/GRU actor-critic (self-/cross-attention, GRU) trained from scratch with PPO, plus a low-level locomotion controller
setting.training_data: Simulation RL only, in Isaac Gym with 4096 parallel envs on one H100, procedurally generated cluttered and maze terrains, ~20k iterations; no pretraining or real data
setting.observation: Proprioception (joint encoders, IMU; 46-d) at 10 Hz and 200 Hz plus 8-frame 30x43 depth history; goal given only at t=0
setting.action_space: Egocentric twist commands [vx, vy, wz] at 10 Hz, tracked by a 50 Hz locomotion controller
setting.privileged: none at test time (privileged sim states and critic maps used only in training); real-world evaluation uses LiDAR Faster-LIO only for scoring, not as policy input

numbers_note: Real-world results (final distance, success in 10 trials per setting) are given only in a figure, so not captured. Sim benchmarks are the authors' own procedurally generated terrains, not standard public benchmarks.
results: GUIDE reaches 99.6-99.9% SR across four simulated settings with the goal given only at start. It beats SRU, which receives streaming GT goals (e.g. Maze Hard 99.6 vs 76.3 SR), and GUIDE-Legolas (63.3 on Maze Hard). It is within ~0.4 points of the GT oracles and transfers zero-shot to a Lite3 quadruped (trajectories up to 56.1 m; final distance ~0.2-0.3 m).
limitations: Occasionally misses traversable openings in confined spaces due to the limited field of view of the depth sensor.
Small remaining gap to GT oracles shows learned internal state is imperfect; scalability to much larger-scale navigation is untested.
Evaluated on self-generated simulated terrains and small real-world trial counts (10 per setting), with no standard benchmark comparison.
builds_on: Hybrid internal model locomotion (Long et al.)
